title: What are Props?
overview: Props (short for Properties) are used to pass data from a parent component to a child component. They allow components to become reusable by displaying different data without changing the component's internal code.

title: Why Do We Use Props?
overview: Props make components dynamic and reusable. Instead of creating multiple components with similar functionality, you can create one component and pass different values using props.

example.title: Real-World Example
example.content: Imagine a User Card component. Instead of creating a separate card for every user, you can pass different names, images, and ages through props.

title: Passing Multiple Props
overview: A component can receive multiple props at the same time. Each prop represents a different piece of information that the component can display or use.

title: Destructuring Props
overview: Instead of accessing every prop using props.name or props.age, you can destructure props directly in the function parameters. This makes your code shorter and easier to read.

title: Props are Read-Only
overview: Props cannot be modified by the child component. They are read-only because the parent component owns the data. If the data needs to change, the parent component should update it and pass the new value again.

example.title: Example
example.content: Props are like function parameters. The child component can use them but should never change them.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what props are, why they are important, how to pass single and multiple props, how to destructure them, and why props should never be modified inside child components.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Props pass data from parent to child.
✔ Props make components reusable.
✔ Multiple props can be passed.
✔ Destructuring makes code cleaner.
✔ Props are read-only.
